brief: UBS sales desk commentary covering three macro catalysts ahead of a Fed-sensitive day. US: Waller said a core CPI print of 0.3% or higher warrants a 50bps hike; that remark already repriced the December Fed meeting to roughly 25bps, closing a gap open since April, the last time core printed above 30bps. UBS's own core forecast has converged near consensus (26bps/23bps vs 27bps/22bps), its nowcast sees a hotter headline (+32bps) but cooler core (+22bps), and the share of CPI basket items rising above 2% keeps declining. Canada: today's BoC deliberations summary covers the year's first 25bps hike; UBS sees the BoC, now in the lower part of its 2.25%-3.25% neutral range, reaching the 2.75% midpoint, with OIS pricing roughly two more hikes over the next year split between December and January. No FX view currently, but a retrace toward 1.43 diverging from macro pricing would make another short USDCAD appropriate. Sweden: Riksbank's hawkish minutes (SWESTR curve 5bps cheaper) frame September's softer inflation as travel-price noise with underlying pressure still rising, and flag more hikes may be needed to stop inflation settling above target; UBS holds a standing short USDSEK.
